But it isn't her. My mom never once asked me to stay. Not even at the dock. She wanted to, I _saw_ her want to. She gave me Dad's compass and she let me go.
That's who you are, Mom. Not this. I'm going to get you back to who you are.
Then I will make you stay.
The light gutters. The shadow that was wound around her peels away like wet paper, and burns, and is gone.
What is left is a tired woman kneeling on a stone floor, holding a lamp that is still, somehow, alight.
Oh. Look at you. You've grown. You— your _hair_. You cut it yourself, didn't you. It's terrible.
_(laughing, and not laughing)_ Ilse did the back.
I did my best, Keeper. She wouldn't hold still.
She never would.
How long?
A year. I meant to hold it for a minute. Just until the boat was clear.
Something took hold of me afterwards. It kept saying, _not yet. Not yet. Keep her safe._ I think it was me. I'm sorry. I think it was only ever me.
I'm sorry. I'm sorry I took the Dawnstone. I'm sorry about what I said at supper. I'm sorry I left. I'm sorry I didn't come home sooner—
Wren. Little bird. Breathe.

I knew you would leave from the day you could walk. I wasn't angry that you wanted to go. I was angry that I was so afraid of it. Those aren't the same thing. It took me sixteen years and the end of the world to see it.
You went out after Dad. That night. I found your hand-lamp, tied to the Gull's Return.
...You found it.

I left the Lantern dark for two hours. The only two hours in two hundred years. I looked for him until the oil ran out. Then I rowed home, because you were asleep in the house, and someone had to keep the light on for you.
You never told me. I thought for seven years you didn't even try.
I know. I let you think it. It was easier to be the villain than to be the one who wasn't enough.
I always thought you could have saved Dad. I thought it for seven years.
I know you did. I tried, Wren. Some day you might find out how hard. Don't hate me for not telling you.
I never hated you. I was just— sixteen.
I remember sixteen. It's dreadful. I wouldn't do it twice for all the light in the world.
Ilse. You kept her alive. I can see you did.
...Someone had to carry the bandages.
Squire Kestrel. Late again.
Don't be. You came.
And you have a name now, I think. A real one.
Sable. Wren gave it to me. I kept it.
Good. Keep it. Keep it the way you'd keep a promise.
I'm Pip. I'm— a friend. Of hers. I steal things.
Then you're welcome in my house, Pip. Don't steal the spoons. They were my mother's.
Bring them home.
They're not mine to bring.
They are now.
Now. The light.
She holds out the lamp. Inside the brass, where the Dawnstone used to sleep, a piece of the broken sun.
A Keeper's light can't go out while the Keeper holds it. So I'm going to stop holding it. And you're going to carry it instead.
I don't know how to be a Keeper. I never learned the Lantern. I left before you could teach me.
Oh, Wren. A Keeper isn't a lighthouse. A Keeper is someone who keeps a light going for the people still out in the dark. You've been doing it all year. I watched.
Not here. Not this island. Wherever you go.
Wren carries the Lanternkeeper's light. The *Lanternkeeper* Crest can now be equipped.
There. Oh, that's better. My hands were so tired.
I have to, little bird. That's the whole point. That's what I was too afraid to learn.
I'm trying.
I know. I can tell.
And for the first time in a year, the Lantern of Lanternfall goes out.
For a moment there is nothing at all.
Then, in Wren's open hand, a small warm light. It does not need a Lantern.
...She was nice. Your mum.
She was terrible. She was the best.
Both. She was both.
Yeah. Both is allowed.

I said goodbye to Mom. A real one, this time. She said a Keeper is someone who keeps a light going for people out in the dark. Then she let go, and the Lantern went out, and the light was in my hand. Grow up well, she said. I'm trying.
The Lantern log of Lanternfall, open on its stand, two hundred years of weather and oil in neat columns. One page is creased, as if it has been opened to many times.
_14th of Harvest. Keeper absent from the lamp, second bell to fourth. Keeper at sea in search of the fishing boat Gull's Return, lost with one aboard. — Y.H._
And below it, in a hand that is not quite steady: _Lamp relit at fourth bell. Wren asleep. Did not find him. Do not tell her._
...She went out. Keepers never leave the Lantern. She went out after him.
